title: Telemetry-driven admission gating and attention fanout for tail mitigation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: under realistic mixed workloads we observe outlier prefill+decode tail latency spikes driven by mismatched kernel paths and attention memory pressure. Existing continuous-batching admission is conservative or coarse-grained: it either admits too aggressively (causing kernel thrashing and long P99s) or too restrictively (losing throughput).

Goal: implement a telemetry-driven admission gating layer that shapes incoming prefill requests using lightweight attention-fanout estimates and kernel-fit scoring to reduce P99 prefill latency by ~30% under 95th percentile load while preserving >=95% baseline throughput. The feature should integrate with our kernel selection hints so runtime can prefer quantized/streaming kernels when appropriate and trigger prefetch/warmup for attention-heavy requests.

Approach:
1) Signal design: derive per-request signals in the front proxy and serving layer — estimated attention-fanout (tokens * avg-attention-sparsity), kv-cache-size estimate, recent kernel-miss-rate, and short-window tail-quantiles for decode latency. Emit these as compact telemetry keys (labels + numeric).
2) Admission scorer: implement a lightweight scoring function in the admission controller that maps telemetry to an admission class: fast-pass, shaped-pass, delayed-pass, or reject. Rules are deterministic by default (configurable thresholds) and support an optional learned policy (logistic model trained offline) for high-variance traffic.
3) Kernel hints coupling: admission outputs kernel_hint metadata for the runtime scheduler (e.g., prefer_streaming_kernel, prefer_quantized, prewarm_attention). The scheduler uses kernel_hint to pick kernels and to schedule prefill vs. decode ordering.
4) Batch shaping: when shaped-pass is chosen, the admission controller assigns a batch-shape profile (micro-window size, max tokens per slot, deadline slack) to the request. The batch shaper aggregates compatible profiles to create shaped minibatches that respect attention memory budgets.
5) Prefill/Decode scheduling: add a prefill-priority lane that admits attention-heavy requests slightly earlier in prefill to allow KV prewarm and reduce kernel handoff overhead during decode. Also add a decode-priority backoff when kernel contention is high.
6) Observability and rollout: add dedicated dashboards (P50/P90/P99 prefill and decode latencies, kernel-miss-rate, admission-class distribution) and an A/B canary with synthetic heavy-tailed prompt sets.

Tradeoffs and constraints: deterministic rules are simple and debuggable but can underperform on complex distributions; learned policy improves decisions but requires offline training and feature stability. Kernel hints require coordination with runtime teams to ensure no excessive kernel switching. Memory-limited GPUs may require stricter shaping thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: New telemetry keys emitted for attention-fanout, kv-cache-size-est, and kernel-miss-rate with <0.5ms extraction overhead
Admission controller returns one of {fast-pass, shaped-pass, delayed-pass, reject} for >99% requests in canary traffic
End-to-end P99 prefill+decode latency reduced by >=30% on heavy-tailed synthetic workload compared to baseline (measured over 24h)
Throughput maintained at >=95% of baseline on mixed production traffic during canary window
Kernel_hint tags propagate to runtime and at least one kernel path (streaming or quantized) is selected for >70% of shaped-pass requests in canary
Observability: dashboard surfaces admission class breakdown and correlates kernel-miss-rate with P99 spikes
Canary rollout plan and automated rollback if P99 increases >10% or error rate increases >0.5%
updates: 2026-03-02: Triage completed. Scoped to runtime + admission + observability. Assigned to Diego.
2026-03-04: Spike analysis: correlation found between attention fanout > 1.5e6 and kernel-miss-rate jumps. Proposed fanout thresholding as simple initial rule.
2026-03-06: Prototype admission scorer implemented in dev env; deterministic rules only. Measured admit decision latency ~0.9ms including telemetry extraction.
2026-03-09: Kernel hint proto added. Runtime team (Marta Nguyen) confirmed ability to route to streaming kernel via kernel_hint tag. Minor API tweak agreed (hint name -> kernel_hint_v2).
2026-03-11: Benchmark: shaped-pass with prewarm reduced P99 by 28% in synthetic tail workload but throughput dropped 3%. Need to tune shaping profiles to recover throughput.

2026-03-14: Design review with PM and runtime leads. Decided on phased rollout: 1) deterministic rules + dashboards, 2) tuned shaping profiles, 3) optional learned policy. Preparing canary PR and dashboard panels.
